references.text: Dan is born as Bilhah's son, Rachel's maidservant. Here the origin of Dan, one of the sons listed in Exodus 1:4, is mentioned.
Naftali is born as Bilhah's son. Here the origin of Naftali, one of the sons listed in Exodus 1:4, is mentioned.
Gad is born as Zilpah's son, Leah's maidservant. Here the origin of Gad, one of the sons listed in Exodus 1:4, is mentioned.
Asher is born as Zilpah's son. Here the origin of Asher, one of the sons listed in Exodus 1:4, is mentioned.
A complete list of Jacob's sons, including Dan and Naftali (Bilhah's sons) and Gad and Asher (Zilpah's sons).
The sons of Dan and Naftali are mentioned when Jacob's family travels down to Egypt, the same context as Exodus 1.
The sons of Gad and Asher are mentioned when Jacob's family travels down to Egypt, the same context as Exodus 1.
Jacob's blessings over Dan, Gad, Asher, and Naftali before his death, which give prophetic words about these tribes.
Confirms the eternal unity of the twelve tribes through various historical perspectives (exile versus restoration).
Clarifies the theological status of Dan and Naftali as part of Rachel's inheritance tribe through Bilhah.
Connects the identity of the tribes from their origin directly to their role in confirming God's curses toward disobedience.
Completes the story from the patriarchs' origins to their prophetic inheritance in the new creation.
